name: Blood Orange
label: RCA / Domino
lede: Dev Hynes was 18 and screaming in Test Icicles, then a folk singer called Lightspeed Champion, then Blood Orange, writing for Solange, Carly Rae Jepsen and Blondie. In 2025 Pitchfork put his grief record Essex Honey at No. 24 of the year.

eras.title: Eighteen, screaming, and done in two years
eras.text: Dev Hynes joined two people he knew from London's clubs in a dance-punk band, put out one album and watched it end in February 2006.

years.h: Hynes joins a band called Balls, and it becomes Test Icicles
years.p: Rory Attwell and Sam Mehran had played with Ferry Gouw until he left for Indonesia. They recruited Dev Hynes, who was 18, from the London club scene, including the Afterskool night.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Gouw suggested the new name. Hynes played guitar, synth and the odd vocal, in a sound it lists as dance-punk crossed with post-hardcore, run through Peavey and Fender amps.

years.h: Test Icicles' only album puts two singles in the UK top 40
years.p: For Screening Purposes Only came out October 31, 2005. "Circle. Square. Triangle" reached No. 25 and "What's Your Damage" No. 31.
years.xp: The album itself peaked at No. 69 in the UK. It was the band's whole studio catalogue.

years.cap: Test Icicles on stage, February 5, 2006, the month the split was announced
years.h: Three months after the album, Test Icicles split
years.p: The band announced the breakup in February 2006. The farewell EP Dig Your Own Grave, remixes and videos, followed on April 26.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Mehran later moved to New York and worked in music, and died in July 2018. It gives no cause. Attwell kept releasing music under other names.

eras.title: Lightspeed Champion drops the scream
eras.text: Hynes took a name from comic strips he'd drawn in school maths books, made a folk record in Nebraska and wrecked his throat touring it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion · Wikipedia: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge
years.h: A London screamer flies to Omaha to make a folk record
years.p: In early 2007 he records at ARC Studios with Saddle Creek producer [[Mike Mogis|0306016b-331c-4519-b51e-f11dfc217455]], backed by locals including the Faint's Clark Baechle and Emmy the Great.
years.xp: The name Lightspeed Champion comes from comic strips Hynes drew as a teenager in his school maths books, per Wikipedia. Trumpeter Nate Walcott and members of Cursive and Tilly and the Wall also played on the record.

years.h: "Galaxy of the Lost" goes out as the first single
years.p: It comes out July 30, 2007, six months ahead of the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge
years.h: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge is named for a toy frog
years.p: A lavender frog his mother gave him as a child to help him sleep. Domino puts the album out January 21 and it reaches No. 45 in the UK.
years.xp: Hynes described the record as a mixture of his dreams and life experiences, per Wikipedia. Critics split: Pitchfork gave it 6.3 and NME 9 out of 10.

years.cap: Hynes with Lightspeed Champion at the Leadmill, Sheffield, 2008
years.h: Florence Welch and Emmy the Great play in his live band
years.p: Violinist Mike Siddell and drummer Anna Prior fill out the lineup. Alex Turner and Faris Badwan sit in as guests, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion · Wikipedia: Coastal Grooves
years.h: Two years of touring wreck his throat
years.p: Wikipedia says Hynes had serious damage and needed extensive surgery. He stayed off the road for about two and a half years.
years.xp: The second album, Life Is Sweet! Nice to Meet You, came out in 2010. Hynes then retired Lightspeed Champion to focus on Blood Orange. Wikipedia's Coastal Grooves page ties his falsetto on the next record to the surgery.

eras.title: Blood Orange, and a Solange EP
eras.text: Hynes had lived in New York since 2007. In late 2009 he started playing as Blood Orange, an R&B and electronica project, and by 2012 he was co-writing for Solange.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: Blood Orange plays its first shows in New York and London
years.p: Hynes does the first sets in November and December 2009, after two years in the city.
years.xp: On December 17, 2009, he performed "Forget It" on the final episode of MTV's It's On with Alexa Chung, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Blood Orange at the Shacklewell Arms, London, December 4, 2011
years.h: "Dinner" is the first Blood Orange single
years.p: It comes out in January 2011 on Terrible Records, the label Solange would also join.
years.xp: "Sutphin Boulevard" turned up on the January 17, 2011 premiere of MTV's Skins, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Coastal Grooves · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: Ariel Rechtshaid produces Coastal Grooves in Los Angeles
years.p: Domino puts it out in August and sells it as New York in the 1980s. Pitchfork gives it 5.9; Metacritic averages 72.
years.xp: "Champagne Coast" went viral on TikTok in July 2024, thirteen years on, and reached No. 15 on Billboard's Hot Alternative Songs chart, according to Wikipedia. On April 9, 2012, Hynes opened a tour for Florence and the Machine.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dev Hynes · Wikipedia: Solange Knowles
years.h: He co-writes and co-produces [[Solange Knowles|410e7fd3-b865-4fa0-bb18-1b7fd53382ca]]'s True
years.p: The EP is Solange's first for Terrible Records and reaches iTunes on November 27, 2012.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Hynes as co-writer and co-producer of True. The same year he wrote "Everything Is Embarrassing" for [[Sky Ferreira|05f3353e-e2d9-4344-a3c9-8009dd8e0427]].

years.cap: Hynes at the Brooklyn Night Bazaar
years.src: Wikipedia: Cupid Deluxe · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: Cupid Deluxe, written after he moves from Brooklyn to Manhattan
years.p: Eleven tracks, with Caroline Polachek, David Longstreth, Skepta and Clams Casino. Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and later ranks it No. 35 among the 2010s' top albums.
years.xp:
Hynes called it a record about life transitions, going from a stable position to an unstable one. The Fader put him on the cover of issue 89 that month, and the album streamed on YouTube on November 5, 2013.

It also holds a cover of Mansun's "I Can Only Disappoint U", retitled "Always Let You Down".

years.h: He scores Gia Coppola's Palo Alto
years.p: It's his first film score, six years before Queen & Slim.

eras.title: Two records, two years apart, and pop on the side
eras.text: Freetown Sound came out in 2016 and Negro Swan in 2018. Around them, Hynes wrote songs for Carly Rae Jepsen and Blondie.

years.h: Carly Rae Jepsen records "All That" and "Body Language"
years.p: Hynes co-wrote and co-produced "All That" for [[Carly Rae Jepsen|09887aa7-226e-4ecc-9a0c-02d2ae5777e1]]'s Emotion and co-wrote "Body Language" for Emotion: Side B.

years.cap: Blood Orange at Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 16, 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Freetown Sound · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: Freetown Sound comes out three days early
years.p: He moved it up from July 1. The title is Freetown, Sierra Leone, his father's birthplace; it samples writer Ta-Nehisi Coates and slam poet Ashlee Haze, and Pitchfork gave it 8.8.
years.xp:
Hynes announced the album on April 18, 2016. Guests include Carly Rae Jepsen, Nelly Furtado, Debbie Harry, Kelsey Lu and Empress Of.

Wikipedia says IMPALA shortlisted it for its 2016 Album of the Year, and it peaked at No. 159 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: He writes "Long Time" with Deborah Harry for Blondie
years.p: On Pollinator, it reaches No. 5 on Billboard's Hot Dance chart and No. 19 on Adult Alternative Songs.

years.cap: Hynes at the Danforth Music Hall, Toronto, October 1, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Negro Swan · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: Hynes puts black depression on Negro Swan
years.p: Out August 24. He described it as an honest look at the corners of black existence and the anxieties of queer people of color. Puff Daddy, A$AP Rocky and Steve Lacy guest.
years.xp: Hynes announced it July 19, 2018, and the first two singles, "Charcoal Baby" and "Jewelry", followed that week. Pitchfork gave it 7.6 and ranked it No. 46 of 2018. Metacritic scored it 84.

years.h: Fields with Third Coast Percussion earns a Grammy nomination
years.p: It's up for Best Chamber Music/Small Ensemble Performance. The same year he scores Queen & Slim.
years.xp: His mixtape Angel's Pulse came out on July 12, 2019, after he announced it to Cultured Magazine on June 25.

eras.title: The film scorer, and a song with a second life
eras.text: Hynes scored films and a Broadway play and played Philip Glass at Carnegie Hall, while a 2011 song of his found a new audience on TikTok.

years.h: He scores We Are Who We Are, Mainstream, Passing and Master Gardener
years.p: Wikipedia also lists his performances of Philip Glass's piano Etudes at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center.

years.h: Hynes signs to RCA and plays The Tonight Show
years.p: The Four Songs EP follows in 2022.

years.h: Job brings him to Broadway
years.p: He writes the music for the play.

years.src: Wikipedia: Coastal Grooves · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: TikTok finds "Champagne Coast" thirteen years late
years.p: The 2011 song from Coastal Grooves climbs to No. 15 on Hot Alternative Songs.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists him at Coachella on April 10 and 17, 2026, playing "Champagne Coast" and "Bad Girls".

eras.title: Essex, and grief
eras.text: Essex Honey took on grief and the Essex he came from, with Lorde, Caroline Polachek and Zadie Smith as guests.

years.src: Wikipedia: Essex Honey · Wikipedia: Blood Orange (musician)
years.h: "The Field" leads off Essex Honey over a Durutti Column sample
years.p: Out June 26, 2025, with Caroline Polachek and Daniel Caesar. "Somewhere in Between" and "Mind Loaded" follow on July 17, the day the album is announced.

years.h: Hynes produces the Charlatans
years.p: Wikipedia credits him with producing the British band's 2025 album We Are Love.

years.cap: Blood Orange at Way Out West, Gothenburg
years.h: Pitchfork puts Essex Honey at No. 24 of 2025
years.p: Hynes writes, produces and engineers it himself, on RCA and Domino. Pitchfork gives it 8.1; Metacritic averages 88, and NME, the Guardian and Rolling Stone give five stars.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Hynes made it during a period of "collective grief and loss", drawing on Elliott Smith and the Replacements. Guests include Lorde, Caroline Polachek, Daniel Caesar, Mustafa the Poet, Brendan Yates of Turnstile, Ben Watt, Tirzah, Zadie Smith and Amandla Stenberg. "Countryside" was the last single, on August 27.

Bijan Stephen of The Nation called it "wonderfully vulnerable and occasionally joyous." It reached No. 69 on the UK albums chart.

yt: Full Toronto show, Essex Honey tour
years.h: Autumn on the road with Lorde and Turnstile
years.p: Hynes supports [[Lorde|8e494408-8620-4c6a-82c2-c2ca4a1e4f12]]'s Ultrasound World Tour and Turnstile's Never Enough Tour.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists a North American and European tour that autumn.
